correctness.rationale: The complete metric inequalities reduce exactly to |s|<=t, |x_i|<=1, |x_i-s|<=1. Fiber slicing gives intervals [s-1,1] for s>=0 and [-1,s+1] for s<=0. Interior fiber variables perturb independently; interior hub levels perturb affinely, leaving only -t,0,t. Each boundary-layer corner is truly extreme; at s=0 any leaf at ±1 forces both summands hubs to have the sign of their average zero, hence 0. For 0<t<2 all three fibers have 2^n corners; at t=2 extreme endpoint fibers are singletons. Polar duality yields exact primal facet counts. Standalone exact spanning-tree checker passed all 18 n,t cases; finite checks are not the uniform proof.

value.rationale: A standard n-page book graph has a natural continuous hub-shortcut deformation; dual-polytope extreme points/facet counts are invariantly meaningful for Lipschitz-free Banach-space geometry. The result gives an exact entire continuum of weighted metrics, all dimensions n>=2, an exhaustive three-layer description and a sharp combinatorial transition losing 2^(n+1)-2 facets at t=2. This extends rather than repeats the known fixed unweighted book graph count; no unrelated parameters or arbitrary finite slice are selected.
